name: Duration change, tested and checked
purpose: Complete formatDuration in src/duration.ts of the isolated experiment repository so that the existing tests in test/duration.test.ts pass, without editing any test file and without adding dependencies. One agent makes the change, DSpatch runs the tests itself, and a second agent judges the change against the real test result. This is not the external DSpatch development loop and not the chat loop.
notes: DSP-139. Why DSpatch runs the test here rather than an agent: Niclas's mandate of 27 October 2026 chose gate steps in which DSpatch runs an explicitly configured build or test command, and no command tool for Claude. So the agent steps only read and edit, the gate runs the command, and the check step is handed the gate's real record (command, folder, exit code or signal, bounded output, the run, the visit and the snapshot it tested). The command is not a field of this file: the drawing format has none, and the editor's Run binds it in code for this one bundled drawing (EXAMPLE_GATE_COMMAND in app/src/shared/loop-editor-run.ts), shown in the gate's panel and named in its purpose. This is a bundled drawing declaring its own gate, not a Command field in ordinary chat: the chat loop and Use loop do not change, nobody is asked for a command, and pressing Run is the act (INTERACTION_MODEL.md sections 6 and 8). The stale rule: a test result counts only for the snapshot of the working folders it ran against. If the working folders differ from it, or cannot be observed, when the check starts or ends, the check is told so and its outcome is recorded as its whenUndeclared (could-not-check), so a change made after the test cannot end at done. A failing test ends at tests-failed with no rework round. Both agent steps inherit the run's model, so this runs under Claude and under Cursor. Do not point this graph at the DSpatch repository: Run generates an isolated experiment repository.

limits.note: Four calls is the work step, the gate, the check and one spare. Guesses, recorded as guesses.

failureKinds.label: specification error
failureKinds.meaning: The task's premise is wrong and the change cannot be made in place. The run stops rather than inventing a different task.

failureKinds.label: blocked
failureKinds.meaning: A concrete obstacle prevents the work: missing access, or a decision this run cannot make.

nodes.label: Complete formatDuration
nodes.purpose:
Edit src/duration.ts so that the tests in test/duration.test.ts pass; the tests are the specification, so read them. Do not edit any test file and do not add dependencies. You do not need to run the tests: the next step is DSpatch running them. Say what you changed and what you did not establish.

Reply in prose, to the person who reads this run. They may not have read the role and should not have to. If your tools cannot run commands, say which build or test you would have wanted and could not run; where the drawing has a step in which DSpatch runs the project's command itself, that step is where it runs.

`succeeded` means you did the work the mandate asked for, as far as you can tell. `unclear` means you cannot honestly say that — you did not finish, or you cannot tell. Use `unclear` rather than guessing. A later step will check the project; do not treat your own `succeeded` as that check.

Where the step you are in offers `done-unchecked`, it means: the work is done, and the independent check would add nothing, so skip it. It is right only when **you changed no file** and the mandate was a question, a reading or an explanation — the answer is the whole of the work. It is wrong for any change to code, build files, configuration or tests, however small, and wrong whenever you are unsure: then declare `succeeded` and let the check run. Skipping is recorded as skipped, never as checked or met, and the person sees your reason, so the reason is required. Give it on the same line, after the name:

```
RESULT: done-unchecked the mandate was a question about the build; no file changed
```

Where you are offered the tool `request_interactive_handoff`, assess first whether the task benefits from the loop's steps. If working interactively with the person is a better fit — a decision only they can make, or work that has become exploratory — call that tool with a short reason, then end your turn with a short account of where the work stands. Do this before you change files where you can. The person chooses; follow their choice. If they choose to continue in the loop, carry on with the step, and do not recommend the switch again in this run. Never write the recommendation as your outcome or ask for it only in your reply: the tool is the only way it is heard.

If the premise of the mandate is wrong, begin your reply with the word SPEC_ERROR and then one sentence saying what is wrong. If something concrete prevents the work — access you do not have, a decision that is not yours — begin your reply with the word BLOCKED and then one sentence saying what is in the way. Those two words are read only as the opening of your reply, so use either of them freely in ordinary prose anywhere else.

produces.note: Your account of what you changed. The checking step is a different agent with none of this conversation.

nodes.label: DSpatch runs the tests
nodes.purpose: DSpatch runs node --test test/duration.test.ts in the run's working folder. Pass or fail is the process exit code, not an agent's account.

produces.note: DSpatch's record of the command it ran.

nodes.notes: No role and no provider turn. The command is bound to this drawing by the editor's Run (EXAMPLE_GATE_COMMAND), and this purpose names it so a reader sees what will run. Its result is filed and handed to check.

nodes.label: Check the change
nodes.purpose:
Establish whether the assignment was met, from the change in the working folders, the work step's account and the test result DSpatch handed you. That result is evidence about the code version it names and no other. Do not edit files.

Reply in prose, to the person who reads this run. They may not have read the role and should not have to.

DSpatch lets a `met` stand only if a command recorded in this run completed on the code exactly as you leave it, or if the run changed no file. Run your checks on the code as it is, and do not change files.

`met` means the assignment was met. `rework` means it was not met yet and the work step can fix it: list each finding concretely — the command you ran, what it showed, and what has to change — because your reply is the only thing the work step is given about what is wrong. `not-met` means it cannot be met as asked, or what is wrong is not something another round of work would fix; say why. `could-not-check` means you could not establish it — no identifiable check, a command you could not run, or a result you could not read. Use `could-not-check` rather than guessing. It is a real answer and not a failure of the run.

Do not declare `limit-reached`. DSpatch routes that itself when the correction rounds are spent.

If the premise of the check is wrong, begin your reply with the word SPEC_ERROR and then one sentence saying what is wrong. If something concrete prevents the check — access you do not have, a decision that is not yours — begin your reply with the word BLOCKED and then one sentence saying what is in the way. Those two words are read only as the opening of your reply, so use either of them freely in ordinary prose anywhere else.

nodes.label: Change met and tested
nodes.purpose: The tests DSpatch ran passed on the code that was checked, and the checking step declared the assignment met.

nodes.label: Tests failed
nodes.purpose: The command DSpatch ran exited non-zero. Its output is in the record. The change is still in the working copy, and nothing checked it further.

nodes.label: Assignment not met
nodes.purpose: The checking step declared that the assignment was not met. What the work step changed is still in the working copy.

nodes.label: Could not establish
nodes.purpose: The run could not establish whether the assignment was met: the work was unclear, no test command ran, the check could not decide, or the test result did not describe the code that was checked. This is not a pass and not a failure of the project.

nodes.label: Stopped without doing the work
nodes.purpose: The work step reported that the premise was wrong or that it was blocked, so the work was not done and nothing was tested.
